gates.acceptance: current implemented backend capability is represented accurately in UI/landing
gates.evidence: UI and backend currently co-reside largely in WellFit-now, so some alignment exists by construction; the intended WellFit visual repo has not yet received/accepted the canonical UI implementation.

gates.acceptance: native events and backend validation agree; server authority boundaries hold
gates.evidence: Backend Buddy/mission/reward authority exists. The exact Unity source is baselined as an incomplete scaffold/reference set and migration is approved for a fresh destination, but no compile-ready destination, native contract integration or real-device end-to-end proof is accepted.

gates.acceptance: visual/product claims match real native/AR/device evidence
gates.evidence: WellFit-Buddy has a reviewed source baseline but no complete runtime or accepted real-device AR evidence; visual capability claims must remain conservative.

gates.acceptance: one exact-version cross-repo journey passes with current contracts and evidence
gates.evidence: No exact-version three-repository journey has been executed; code ownership is still transitional.

gates.acceptance: verified user session can access protected app flow and server-authoritative mission/economy boundaries remain enforced
gates.evidence: Closed-Beta session hardening PRs #369-#371 plus repository build/database/container gates; this is technical verification, not real-user Production acceptance.

gates.flow: one-screen AR world -> overlay menu -> feature panel -> same AR world
gates.acceptance: on an exact Android build, logo/menu and feature overlays work without intentional AR scene reset; server authority and permission/tracking negative paths remain enforced
gates.evidence: Owner target is specified by WF-CONTRACT-MOBILE-SHELL-001. Runtime, build and device evidence are absent.

rules: Green local repositories do not make an integration gate green.
Integration evidence must bind exact relevant revisions/builds/contracts.
Material contract drift returns affected integration gates to NEEDS_REVALIDATION.
A single-repository gate may record a real technical journey needed by the cross-repo program, but it does not substitute for multi-repository acceptance.
